# SceneService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("SceneService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Reports which scene the game is in and changes to another. A scene is a complete place: its world, its lighting, its UI, its storage services and its own script services. `LoadScene` replaces all of it with another scene between two ticks. `GlobalScriptService` is kept across the change, with its scripts, their variables and their connections.

In a multiplayer match, the authority controls the scene: a host or a server changes it, and every client follows without disconnecting.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CurrentScene` | `Scene` | — | read-only | The scene that is open, as an object that stays valid for that scene. Its `Path` is the path of the scene file relative to the content folder, such as `scenes/arena.scene.json`, or an empty string for a world that no scene file created. After the scene closes, its `IsOpen` returns false. The global `scene` is the same object while the scene is open. |

## Methods

### `GetLoadData(): any`

Returns the `data` that the last `LoadScene` passed, as a fresh copy, or nil.

### `HoldLoading()`

Keeps the loading screen up over a scene until `ReleaseLoading` has been called the same number of times.

The engine shows a loading screen while a scene loads: at the first scene and at every `LoadScene`. It removes the screen once the scene's meshes and images are loaded and the terrain around the camera is meshed. A scene whose scripts build its world, such as generated terrain or parts created from code, should hold the screen until the world is built.

A `ScreenGui` with `KeepOnSceneLoad` on, or one of the new scene's own, is drawn over the engine's loading screen, so a game can show its own. A hold that is never released ends after one minute, with a warning in the log.

### `IsSubWorld(): boolean`

Returns whether this world is running inside another game's `SubWorld`.

### `LoadScene(path: string, data: any? = nil)`

Unloads the current scene and loads the one at `path`, which is relative to the content folder. It returns at once; the change happens at the next safe point between ticks, after `SceneLoading` has fired.

The old scene is removed entirely: its world, the contents and settings of its services, and its scripts, whose threads stop. The new scene starts from the engine's default settings, reads its file, loads its own code from `src/scenes/<scene>/` and starts its scripts.

`data` is passed to the new scene, which reads it with `GetLoadData`. It can hold only plain values, the same as a `RemoteEvent` argument, and no instances. A client connected to a match cannot call this method.

### `LoadSceneAsync(path: string, options: { Activate: boolean?, Data: any? }? = nil): SceneLoad`

Starts preparing the scene at `path` while the current scene keeps running, and returns at once with a `SceneLoad` object. Use its `Progress` for a loading bar, its `Ready` event to know when the scene is prepared, and its `Activate` method to switch.

`options.Activate`, true by default, switches as soon as the scene is ready. Set it to false to wait for a call to `Activate`, for example after a fade or a button press. `options.Data` is the `data` of `LoadScene`.

The switch works like `LoadScene`, with the file already parsed and its meshes already loaded. Only one load runs at a time: a second call cancels the first. A client connected to a match cannot call this method.

### `ReleaseLoading()`

Ends one `HoldLoading`. When none remain, the loading screen is removed as soon as the scene has loaded. Extra calls are ignored.

### `SendToHost(arguments: ...any)`

Inside a `SubWorld`: sends values out to the game that runs this world. The `Received` event of the `SubWorld` fires there with them on its next tick. Use it to report a score or a game over. It accepts the values a `RemoteEvent` accepts, except instances. Raises an error if this world is not inside a `SubWorld`.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `HostMessageReceived(arguments: ...any)`

Inside a `SubWorld`: fires with the values that the game running this world passed to `SubWorld:Send`, one tick after they were sent. It never fires in a world that is not inside a `SubWorld`.

### `SceneLoadFailed(path: string, message: string)`

Fires when a `LoadScene` fails because the scene file does not exist or cannot be read. The scene that was open stays as it was, and its close handlers do not run. `message` gives the reason, which is also logged.

### `SceneLoaded(path: string)`

Fires when the new scene is in place and its scripts have started.

### `SceneLoading(path: string)`

Fires when the scene is about to change to `path`, while the old scene still exists. Show a loading screen here; a `ScreenGui` with `KeepOnSceneLoad` on stays up across the change.
